text: Two underdamped oscillators are known to have the same natural frequency \(\omega_0\). The mass and damping coefficient of the first oscillator are \(m_1\) and \(b_1\), and the mass and damping coefficient of the second oscillator are \(m_2\) and \(b_2\), respectively. A sinusoidal driving force of \(F_{ext}=F_0\cos\omega t\) is applied to each oscillator. Starting with \(\omega\) far from \(\omega_0\) the driving force is tuned in order to observe resonant behavior. If \(m_1=4m_2\) and \(b_1=2b_2\), then which one of the following statements concerning the driven oscillations is CORRECT?

options.A: The resonant peak of the first driven oscillator is higher and narrower than that of the second oscillator
options.B: The resonant peak of the first oscillator is higher and wider than that of the second oscillator
options.C: The resonant peak of the first driven oscillator is lower and wider than that of the second oscillator
options.D: The resonant peak of the first driven oscillator is lower and narrower than that of the second oscillator

text: There exists a uniform electric field \(E\hat{j}\) and a uniform magnetic field \(B\hat{k}\) and no gravitational field in region of space. A particle at origin of mass m, charge +q is given velocity \(\vec{v}_1=+\dfrac{E\hat{i}}{B}\) or \(\vec{v}_2=\dfrac{+\sqrt{3}E\hat{j}}{B}\) at t = 0. Then choose the CORRECT option(s)

options.A: For particle velocity \(\vec{v}_1=+\dfrac{E\hat{i}}{B}\), electric force is balanced by magnetic force.
options.B: For particle velocity \(\vec{v}_2\), particle will attain maximum y – coordinate for the first time at \(\dfrac{2\pi m}{3qB}\)
options.C: For particle velocity \(\vec{v}_2\), maximum y – coordinate is \(\dfrac{3mE}{qB^2}\).
options.D: For particle velocity \(\vec{v}_2\), minimum y – coordinate is \(\dfrac{-mE}{qB^2}\)

In the arrangement shown in figure, weight A possesses mass m, a symmetric pulley B possesses mass M. Also known are the moment of inertia I of the pulley relative to its axis and the radii of the pulley R and 2R. The mass of the threads is negligible. The acceleration of the weight A after the system is set free from rest is given by \(a=\dfrac{3g\left(pM+qm\right)}{\left(rM+sm+\dfrac{I}{R^2}\right)}\). Where p,q,r,s are integers. Find the value of p + q + r + s.

Find the time period (in sec) of small oscillations of a mathematical pendulum of length \(\ell\) if its point of suspension O moves relative to the Earth’s surface in an arbitrary direction with a constant acceleration w (figure). It is given that \(\ell\) = 21 cm, w = \(\dfrac{g}{2}\), and the angle between the vectors \(\vec{w}\) and \(\vec{g}\) equals \(\beta=120^\circ\). (Take g = \(10\,\mathrm{m/s^2}\))

In accordance with classical electrodynamics an electron moving with acceleration \(\vec{w}\) loses its energy due to radiation as \(\dfrac{dE}{dt}=-\dfrac{2e^2}{3c^3}w_{avg.}^2\), where e is the electron charge, c is the speed of light, \(w_{avg.}\) is the average of magnitude of acceleration of the electron. The time during which the energy of an electron of mass m performing almost harmonic oscillations with frequency \(\omega\) becomes \(\dfrac{1}{\eta}\) times is given by \(\dfrac{xmc^y}{2e^2\omega^z}\ln\left(\eta\right)\) where x, y, z are integers. Find the value of \(\dfrac{xy}{z}\).

A uniform rod of mass M and length L is hinged at its lower end on a table. The rod can rotate freely in vertical plane and there is no friction at the hinge. A solid spherical ball of mass M and radius \(R=\dfrac{L}{3}\) is placed in contact with the vertical rod and a horizontal force F is applied at the upper end of the rod. The horizontal component of hinge force acting on the rod immediately after force F starts acting is \(\dfrac{xF}{y}\). Where x, y are co-primes. Find the value of x + y.
(Assume floor is sufficiently rough and the rod is smooth)
